note: Uprise World — the design of record. A small planet from the Heal the 3 album cover: one hemisphere healed, one scorched, a gold seam between them. YOU START ON THE HEALED SIDE. That side is America — the Connecticut and Georgia landmarks, drawn from photographs of real streets that are standing and intact, which is why they belong in a world that is standing and intact. You play a fellow. You check in at four real places tied to four real documents, and the fourth one opens the far side: THE DEEP END, also called THE THREE — the third world, Ukraine and Russia, still burning. You have to earn the right to see it. Every check-in unlocks the next song. There is no ending; walk back and the playlist starts over. Multiplayer is out of scope while this is a static site. This file is the single source of truth for the build — the renderer reads it, so the world can be re-tuned without touching engine code.

healed.holds: all four landmarks — Bridgeport, Hartford, Atlanta, and the Shiloh corner
healed.look: green cover, running water, canopy, clear sky, doves
healed.why: The landmarks are modelled from Google Street View and aerial photography of streets that are standing. Putting them on a scorched hemisphere fought their own reference material. Here the environment matches the source, which makes every building easier to draw and truer to the place.

scorched.calls: the Deep End, or the Three
scorched.holds: Ukraine and Russia — the far side of the world
scorched.look: cracked ground, lava seams, ash sky, dead trees, smoke — all the hellfire, kept
scorched.why: Heal the 3rd World. You do not begin in the wreckage; you begin comfortable, and the wreckage is what you unlock. Ukraine is the part of the world that is actually being destroyed right now, so it is the part that is actually burning here.

world.seam: a glowing gold meridian between the two faces, taken from the album art
world.traversal: spherical gravity — down is always the planet's core, so you can walk any direction and never fall off. Press and drag anywhere to walk, on desktop and on iPhone alike; WASD and arrows as well on desktop. The seam is a wall until 4/4: walk at it before then and the ground turns you back.
world.inversion: This is a deliberate reversal of the first design, which started you in the wreckage and made the green side the prize. Starting healed and unlocking the ruin says the thing the album says. The hellfire terrain is unchanged — it was not deleted, it moved to the side you have to earn.

landmarks.name: Shiloh Baptist Church and the transmission corridor
landmarks.document: Connecticut Siting Council, Docket 516 / 516R — the win
landmarks.outcome: The Council denied United Illuminating's application 5-3 on October 16, 2025, and closed Docket 516R on February 5, 2026 after rejecting the appeal. Reporting recorded the community's unified front as a major factor.
landmarks.refsNote: Five Google views of Shiloh Baptist Church, 477 Broad St. aerial-wide-corridor.jpg is a STREET VIEW frame from Broad Street dated November 2020, not an aerial, and it is the ground truth for the building; the other four are overhead. The church fronts Broad Street with its main ridge PARALLEL to it, the white roof cross on the street-facing slope and solar panels on the back slope; the Delvis Furniture warehouse at 466 Lafayette Street fills the block behind it. The owner then supplied a Street View walk of the property (Nov 2020 and Jul 2024 imagery), which is what settled the corner-lot orientation, the basketball court in the parking lot, and the elevated stone embankment.
landmarks.note: The environmental-justice case he actually won is the thing that heals the planet. This is the payoff and should be built last and best.
landmarks.project: Fairfield to Congress Railroad Transmission Line 115-kV Rebuild: relocation of UI's existing 115-kV circuits off the railroad catenary structures onto new steel monopoles 95 to 145 feet tall, along about 7.3 miles of the CTDOT Metro-North corridor between Sasco Creek in Fairfield and the Congress Street Substation in Bridgeport.
landmarks.scale: The monopoles are built to the docket's real 95-145 feet against a steeple of about fifty. That ratio is the argument the level makes.
landmarks.cornerLot: 477 Broad Street is a CORNER LOT at Broad Street x Railroad Avenue, signalised. The front gable, the recessed porch and the steeple face BROAD STREET; the long flank runs back along RAILROAD AVENUE, so the ridge is perpendicular to Broad Street. The parking lot between that flank and Railroad Avenue is painted as a BASKETBALL COURT - blue key, orange trim, light-blue apron - with a backboard and hoop on a pole at the church end. The white roof cross lies on the slope facing that court; the solar array is on the other slope.
landmarks.embankment: The railroad is NOT in a cut. It rides an ELEVATED EMBANKMENT behind a rough-cut STONE RETAINING WALL along the far side of Railroad Avenue, with the steel catenary lattice standing on the deck above. Railroad Avenue passes under the tracks at the far end. The Docket 516 monopoles stand up on that deck, which is why 95 to 145 feet reads the way it does from the church door.
landmarks.rights: The owner states the property is theirs and that this use is permitted.
landmarks.placement: Last of the four and nearest the seam. It is the one that opens the Deep End, so it stands on the healed side at the threshold, looking across.

people.note: The record, handed over by the people who actually issued it. Three bodies recognised this work independently and none of them corresponded with any other, so this is collection, not a relay: gather the three honours in any order and carry them to Shiloh, where the case they are about was fought and won.
people.realPeopleRule: These are real, living public officials, named because they really signed these documents. Two hard rules follow. FIRST: no invented opinions. Every line a named official speaks is restricted to what their own document actually says — the honour, its date, its subject. They never endorse the game, the album, a politician, or anything outside the four corners of the paper they signed, and they never comment on Docket 516. SECOND: no likenesses. The rig is a stylised low-poly figure and no attempt is made to resemble anyone's face, build, or colouring; identity is carried by the nameplate and title, never by the model. Do not 'improve' this by sourcing photographs and sculpting faces.
people.accuracy: Read off the scans in assets/credentials/img/, not from memory. Bridgeport is ONE proclamation from Mayor Joseph P. Ganim. Hartford is THREE citations introduced by nine legislators and signed by the President Pro Tempore, the Speaker of the House and the Secretary of the State, given October 5 2025 at the State Capitol. Atlanta is ONE proclamation from Governor Brian P. Kemp. Shiloh is the Docket 516 / 516R decision, which was won and issued to nobody. A keeper who miscounts the citations discredits the record this world exists to carry.
people.carryRule: You may hold all three honours at once and collect them in any order. Shiloh takes whatever you arrive with. No timer, no fail state, nothing to drop.
people.performance: A full character rig is 14,440 triangles — eleven of them is twelve times the planet. So only the person who speaks gets a full rig; a delegation standing with them is built at strands:0 (5,080 tris), and every site's people are hidden until you are near that site. Cost is bounded by whichever landmark you are standing at, not by the total cast.

people.sourcing: Names, titles and spellings on this cast are checked against public record — the credential scans in assets/credentials/img/ for the signatories, and published sources for Shiloh. Where a description we were given conflicts with the record, the record wins and the conflict is written down rather than quietly smoothed over. See delegationNote on the Shiloh entry.

audio.loadPolicy: Each track downloads only when its landmark unlocks it. Files are 4-5MB and the audience is on metered plans; nobody pays for a song they have not reached.

scorched.why: The far side is called the Deep End, and Deep End is what plays when you get there.

healed.behaviour: Heal the 3rd World repeats alone until the first check-in — it names the job before you have done any of it. Each unlock adds the next track to the rotation. Returning to this side always restarts the playlist from the top.
healed.gap: Heal the 3rd World has NO timed lyrics, and it is now the OPENING track, so the lyric rail is empty until the first check-in. That was a quiet gap on the old reward side; here it is the first thing anyone sees. Running it through DistroKid closes it. If that cannot happen soon, swap the opener to Money or the Power, which has cues.

audio.lyrics: Timed lyrics render at the side of the screen, synced to the playhead, using the same cue data the album pages already use.

floor.rule: The 3D world is a layer over the record, never a replacement for it. With WebGL off, on a weak device, with reduced motion, or to a search crawler, the documents stay readable at equity-uprise.html. Nothing here may become the only route to the evidence.
floor.renderer2d: Planned: the same game logic driving a lightweight 2D map for phones that cannot run WebGL. The owner chose to build 3D first; the logic layer is kept separate so the second renderer does not require a rewrite.
floor.reducedMotion: Honour prefers-reduced-motion: no camera shake, no idle drift.

outOfScope: Multiplayer — needs a websocket server; this is a static site.
Photorealistic map tiles — licensing is murky for game use, the payload is fatal on the target phones, and photoreal buildings would fight the cel-shaded art direction.
An ending — the owner asked for none. The only progression is opening the green side.

districts.decision: Owner chose 'landmark + a little context' (not block-accurate city recreation, not one blended capital). The world stays a small walkable planet in the Abeto style.
districts.rule: Each landmark sits in a COMPACT stylized pocket of its real city: the accurate hero building, plus a few surrounding context buildings, a plaza, trees, and street props (lamps, signs, benches, a monument), laid out ROUGHLY like the real overhead map but COMPRESSED to a few walkable steps. Cel-shaded and flat like everything else. The hero building is accurate; the context is stylized filler for atmosphere, never a real-map mesh.

context.bridgeport-city-hall: Lyon Terrace green, McLevy Hall / county buildings nearby, street trees.
context.connecticut-state-capitol: the Capitol grounds + the LOB across the way (both already modelled), Bushnell Park edge, trees.
context.georgia-state-capitol: Liberty Plaza (the oval lawn) opposite the Capitol, the Twin Towers / state office buildings flanking, the Washington St frontage, dense street trees. Overhead map: assets/landmarks/georgia-state-capitol/topdown-map.jpg.
context.docket-516: Shiloh Baptist Church (small powder-blue church, white steeple, cross) beside the rail/transmission corridor with monopoles and overhead lines; the arena dome in the distance. The church stands small against the industrial corridor.

built.record: SURVEY in that module is the geographic record: for each landmark, the compass bearing of the model's +Z axis, every street with its real name and width and which side of the building it lies on, and the findings each fact was read from.
built.convention: A landmark group stands on y = 0 with +Z as its facade direction. frontBearing is the TRUE COMPASS BEARING of +Z, so the model +X axis has bearing frontBearing + 90. Street sides are named front / back / left / right relative to that frame and carry the sign of their offset.
built.streetsNamed: Named streets are built in-world as green blade signs on poles at both ends of every frontage, using the same inked block alphabet the buildings carry.

orientation.docket-516: +Z bearing 340 (NNW). The gable, porch and steeple face Broad Street; Railroad Avenue runs down the right flank past the basketball court; the stone embankment carrying the railroad and the Docket 516 monopoles is beyond Railroad Avenue; the Delvis Furniture warehouse and its mural run along Railroad Avenue behind.
orientation.bridgeport-city-hall: +Z bearing 0 (NORTH). The portico faces Lyon Terrace, with Golden Hill Street the through street beyond it.
orientation.ct-legislative-office-building: +Z bearing 180 (SOUTH). The front faces Capitol Avenue; Broad Street runs down the west flank.
orientation.georgia-state-capitol: +Z bearing 270 (WEST). The grand portico and steps face Washington Street SW. M L King Jr Drive north, Mitchell Street SW south, Capitol Avenue SW east, Liberty Plaza at the north-east corner. Read off the supplied overhead map, which is north-up.

built.correction: Two passes were wrong before this one. First the railroad was laid straight across the front door. Then the church was built with its long side on Broad Street. The owner's Street View walk settled it: it is a corner lot, the gable end is on Broad Street, the long flank and the painted basketball court are on Railroad Avenue, and the railroad is up on a stone embankment across that avenue.
